newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Meyer says no special Sfr target.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Meyer says no special Sfr target.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) president Hans Meyer said the central bank had no specific target for the Swiss franc, but was acting in a flexible way.

"We have no specific aim. We react to those specific developments which we will have to live with for some time to come," Meyer said, briefing journalists at the International Monetary Conference here.

Meyer was responding to a reporter's question about the Swiss central bank's injection of liquidity Wednesday in money markets. The SNB has in recent days been offering liquidity at aggressive rates, following its announcement on May 21 that it would act to counter the Swiss franc's rise.

Meyer also said in response to questions that the biggest potential policy problem Switzerland would face in the foreseeable future would be upward pressure on its currency created by uncertainties tied to European monetary union.
But he was not too concerned that the new "Euro" currency would be weak, and thus have a prolonged negative impact on the Swiss currency.
"I would like to say quite clearly that I think we will have a strong Euro, or no Euro at all," he said.

Meyer said that the central bank had two alternatives to use in addressing the problems it was likely to face in the future: either react in a flexible way, for example, "to try and muddle through at a higher level," or else to peg the Swiss franc to another currency.
But in the case of the latter option, he said one must feel confident the country to which the home currency was pegged was following a policy compatible with one's own.
SNB officials have said in the past that pegging the franc to reduce fluctuations was a measure of last resort.
